parole.significato: Forms pejorative agent nouns.
parole.testo: Probably from Turkish -dir, -dur (cf. Bulgarian чукунду́р (čukundúr, “beetroot”). Formally also matches Proto-Slavic *durь (“idiocity”).

parole.significato: Forms nouns depicting possessor of quality or attribute
parole.testo: Grammaticalization of the Turkish adjectival marker Turkish -li/-lü (when appended to stems with front root vowel), -lı/-lu (when appended to stems with back root vowel). Encountered only with Ottoman Turkish loanwords. Morphologically, the suffix is declined as feminine, however, semantically, the

parole.significato: manufacturing of homespun, homespun tailoring
parole.testo: From Turkish abacılık or an earlier Ottoman form. Alternatively, from абаджи́я (abadžíja) + -лъ́к (-lắk).

parole.significato: bear tamer (someone who entertains others using a tamed bear)
parole.testo: From (the Ottoman Turkish ancestor of) Turkish ayıcı (from ayı + -cı).

parole.significato: A tall, branching grapevine on a trellis.
parole.testo: Derived from Turkish asma.

parole.significato: common bottlenose dolphin, one of three identified species of bottlenose dolphins; Tursiops truncatus
parole.testo: From dialectal Turkish afala, an alternative form of afalina, ultimately from Ancient Greek φάλλαινα (phállaina, “whale”).

parole.significato: well done!, great!
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish aşk olsun.

parole.significato: father, dad (form of address for a father among Muslims)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish baba.

parole.significato: flea market, curios, second-hand market, junk shop
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish bitpazarı (“flea market”, literally “louse-market”), which itself appears to have been modeled on French marché aux puces. Cognate with Macedonian бит-пазар (bit-pazar).

parole.significato: grayish brown (color)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish boz + -ав (-av), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *boŕ.

parole.significato: bosh, humbug, nonsense
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish boş laf (literally “empty talk”), from boş (“empty”) + laf (“word, talk”).

parole.significato: bargain
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish dalavere (“scam”) or Greek νταραβέρι (ntaravéri, “transaction, relationship, commotion”), from the clipping of Italian dare (“giving”) + avere (“taking”). Akin to Macedonian далавера (dalavera), Laz დალავერა (dalavera), Armenian տալավէրա (talavēra), Greek νταλαβέρα (ntalavéra),

parole.significato: lanky, gangling, tall and clumsy person (usually a young man)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish dangalak (“clumsy, simpleton, blockhead”).

parole.significato: döner kebab, doner kebab (dish of meat roasted on a vertical spit)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish döner.

parole.significato: A person who prepares or sells döner kebabs; döner maker.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish dönerci. By surface analysis, дю́нер (djúner) + -джия (-džija).

parole.significato: scream
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Turkish zılgıt (“threatening, scolding”). By surface analysis, Turkish zılgıt + Bulgarian -ня (-nja).

parole.significato: sheath, scabbard
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish kabı, ezafe of kap (“case, vessel”), as in kılıç kabı (“sabre sheath”), with the graphemic change from ⟨b⟩ to ⟨p⟩ likely due to the influence of sense 1 of the term.

parole.significato: katma (traditional Bulgarian pancake, typically larger and thicker than a standard crepe, made with yeast and baked on…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish katma.

parole.significato: bushel (measure for grain used in the past, ranging from several tens to a hundred kilograms)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish kile.

parole.significato: outlaw, highwayman, vagabond
parole.testo: Borrowed from Balkan Turkish kırcal. Probably equivalent to кър (kăr, “field”) + чалия (čalija, “shameless, immoral”) (literally "nomad, bum unbound by law"). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian крџалија, Romanian cîrjaliu/cârjaliu, Albanian kërxhalliu.

parole.significato: kyopolou (a relish, salad and spread made of roasted eggplants (aubergines) and optionally added bell peppers or tomato…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish köpoğlu (literally “son of a bitch”); the semantic evolution of the term is unclear.

parole.significato: muhallebi (a type of dessert, a creamy pudding made with milk and rice flour, topped with fruit syrup)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish muhallebi.

parole.significato: slovenly or unkempt person; pig
parole.testo: Likely borrowed from Turkish palaçor (“old shabby garment”), from Greek παλιατζούρα (paliatzoúra, “junk; old useless item”).

parole.significato: money, collection, tip (collected by musicians or dancers after their performance)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish parsa, from Italian barsa (“purse”).

parole.significato: chop (a cut of meat, often containing a section of a rib)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish pirzola. Cognate with Albanian përzhollë, Greek μπριζόλα (brizóla).

parole.significato: pier, quay, landing stage, wharf (a structure or place by water where vessels stop, load, unload, or take passengers)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish iskele, ultimately from Italian scala.

parole.significato: fence, paling
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish taraba (“wooden fence; shop-front shutter”), itself from North Levantine Arabic دَرَّابَة (darrābe, “a kind of shop-front shutter”).

parole.significato: tas kebab (dish made of finely chopped lamb, pork or veal meat stewed in a sauce with onions or leek, tomatoes and spic…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Turkish tas kebap, from tas (“bowl”) + kebap (“kebab”); literally "kebab in a bowl".

parole.significato: John Doe, Joe Bloggs, Tom, Dick and Harry (a random person)
parole.testo: From Turkish elements; the филан- (filan-) is said to come from a Turkish word филян (filjan, “some, some one”), and kişi (“person”). The final element is -ия (-ija).
